one_line: Early 17th‑century Thanjavur king and commander in the Battle of Toppur during the Vijayanagara succession struggle.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, medium height with a solid, wiry build and a confident warrior’s posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium brown South Indian complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache, slight pointed beard at chin, strong brows, and a calm, thoughtful default expression with alert eyes.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair tied back in a mid‑length topknot, smooth at the sides; simple gold circlet-style crown with a small central ruby and two short side flanges resting above the forehead, no towering elements.
appearance.costume: Era‑accurate Nayaka court-war attire: a long-sleeved cream-colored cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh, worn under a richly draped deep maroon silk angavastra with subtle gold borders over the left shoulder and across the torso; fitted white cotton churidar-style trousers; a wide golden-yellow silk waist sash (odaippu) wrapped twice with a tied knot slightly off-center; bare feet in simple brown leather sandals; gold kada bangles on both wrists, a short multi-strand gold necklace with a single small ruby pendant, and modest gold stud earrings; a faint sandalwood tilak in a vertical line on the forehead.
appearance.signature: A South Indian steel sword with a gently curving single-edged blade, traditional disc-pommel hilt with simple gold-inlaid floral motifs, carried in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard slung from the waist sash on his left side.

ref_desc: Raghunatha Nayaka is a late-30s South Indian king with medium-brown oval face, black topknot under a low gold circlet, cream tunic, deep maroon silk angavastra, white trousers, golden-yellow waist sash, simple jewellery, and a disc-pommel South Indian sword in a brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Raghunatha Nayaka of Thanjavur: a late-30s South Indian king with a medium-brown oval face, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache and small pointed beard, strong brows, and a calm, thoughtful expression. His thick black hair is tied in a mid-length topknot, crowned by a simple low gold circlet with a small central ruby and short side flanges resting above the forehead; add a faint vertical sandalwood tilak on the forehead. Dress him in a long-sleeved cream cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh, over which a deep maroon silk angavastra with subtle gold borders is draped from the left shoulder across the torso and around the back. He wears fitted white churidar-style trousers and a wide golden-yellow silk waist sash wrapped twice, knotted slightly off-center, from which hangs a plain dark-brown leather scabbard. On his feet are simple brown leather sandals. Add gold kada bangles on both wrists, modest gold stud earrings, and a short multi-strand gold necklace with a small ruby pendant. His signature weapon is a South Indian steel sword with a gently curving single-edged blade and a traditional disc-pommel hilt with minimal gold-inlaid floral motifs, shown sheathed at his left side and also clearly visible unsheathed in at least one pose. Use deep maroon, golden yellow, cream, white, and brown leather as dominant colors, and present him in front, side, and three-quarter views to emphasize consistent face, topknot and circlet, draped garments, waist sash, and sword design.
